note: Application requirements compiled from each school's official admissions pages (Fall 2027 = 2026-27 cycle). Prompt text lives in the Common App member section for some schools and is n.a. here.

mit.platform: MIT's own MyMIT portal (not Common App)
mit.prompts: Short answers: fields of study & what led there; time you did something unexpected; problems you'd tackle at MIT; how you handled an unexpected challenge.
mit.interview: Optional (alumni Educational Council; waived without penalty)
mit.special: Optional SlideRoom creative portfolios; MIT activities form replaces a resume

carnegie-mellon.prompts: Passion behind your major; how you define a successful college experience; anything else to emphasize.
carnegie-mellon.special: CFA portfolio/audition/pre-screen for Architecture, Art, Design, Drama, Music; Drama/Music RD Dec 1

penn.prompts: Thank-you note to someone not yet thanked (50-200 w); how you'll explore community at Penn (50-200 w); one undergraduate-school-specific prompt.
penn.special: Extra essays for coordinated dual-degree programs

cornell.prompts: Engineering is heaviest at 6 essays (2×200w + 4×100w). A&S: passion for learning + College alignment (3000ch). CALS: why this major + why CALS (2500ch). AAP: interests → major, creative project for B.Arch.
cornell.special: Portfolio/design supplement for some programs; optional music supplement

purdue.prompts: How Purdue supports your interests, in and out of the classroom (≤250 w); your reasons for pursuing the major you selected (≤250 w).

penn-state.supp_essay_count: Personal statement encouraged; count not stated
penn-state.prompts: n.a. — prompts on the Common App member section
penn-state.interview: Not offered generally (Schreyer optional interview before Nov 1)
penn-state.special: STARS record via MyPennState; arts auditions/Evidence of Creative Work

rit.fee: $65 (waived for deaf/HoH & ASL-EI prospects who visit)
rit.special: Art portfolio for Art/Design/Film & Animation; audiogram for deaf/HoH applicants

illinois-tech.supp_essay_count: Some Illinois Tech questions optional; count unspecified
illinois-tech.special: Architecture scholarship applicants: one-page essay on studying architecture at Illinois Tech

rpi.prompts: B.S./M.D.: reasons for pursuing medicine. Architecture: why architecture. Electronic Arts/GSAS/Music: interests, goals, and portfolio.
rpi.interview: Not offered domestically (InitialView for intl; optional GLIMPSE video)
rpi.special: Architecture portfolio required; GSAS/Electronic Arts/Music portfolios; optional 60-90s GLIMPSE video

georgia-tech.interview: Not offered (international applicants may send a recorded third-party interview)
georgia-tech.special: Program portfolios may be required/optional; language-proficiency interview for international applicants

uiuc.prompts: Experience from past 3-4 yrs related to first-choice major; goals after Illinois and how the major helps; undeclared: goals/interests + possible majors; second-choice major interest.
uiuc.special: Art & Design portfolio; Dance audition; Music application + audition; Theatre interview + audition/portfolio

michigan.prompts: Contributing to U-M's goal of developing leaders and citizens who challenge the present and enrich the future (100-300 w); what attracts you to your specific college/school and how its curriculum supports your interests (100-500 w).
michigan.special: Portfolio/artistic profile for SMTD, Stamps, Taubman

johns-hopkins.platform: Common App or Coalition on Scoir
johns-hopkins.prompts: What you've learned engaging with people whose experiences differ from yours, and how it shaped your thinking about building bridges and working with others (350 w).
johns-hopkins.special: Optional Schoolhouse.world portfolio; ED Agreement; Certification of Finances for international

maryland.prompts: Choose one of UMD's essay questions to share your personality and experiences.
maryland.special: Activities/awards list or resume required; School of Music supplement + audition

northeastern.special: CAMD creative portfolio encouraged (one only); Performing Arts NYC audition

ohio-state.prompts: Morrill Scholarship applicants answer the MSP prompt.
ohio-state.special: Dance/music auditions and portfolios; Eminence Application; MSP essay

nc-state.platform: Common App or Coalition on Scoir
nc-state.prompts: Explain why you selected the academic program(s) and why you want to study them at NC State (required); Honors: optional essay ≤500 w.
nc-state.counselor_rec: No — counselor endorsements dropped as of fall 2022
nc-state.interview: Not offered generally (Design/some depts interview by invitation)
nc-state.special: Portfolio for studio-based majors via wolfPAW, Nov 1 deadline

unc-chapel-hill.prompts: Both appear on the Common Application; UNC's public pages state the requirement but not the prompt text.

virginia-tech.prompts: n.a. — see the Common App member section
virginia-tech.special: STARS record required for U.S.-educated applicants; Ut Prosim Profile within Common App

florida.supp_essay_count: A few additional short-answer questions in the UF Supplement
florida.prompts: n.a.; Honors adds one essay; Innovation Academy adds one essay
florida.special: Honors/Innovation Academy extra essays; College of the Arts audition; STARS record

olin.prompts: Olin-specific essay; prompt text not published on official pages
olin.special: Optional Instrumental Music Portfolio; optional Schoolhouse.world portfolio

rose-hulman.interview: Not offered for U.S. domestic students (InitialView for intl/abroad)

carleton.prompts: Discuss someone you connect with who is different from you and what's meaningful about those interactions; optional open prompt.
carleton.interview: Optional (early June through Jan 15 of senior year)
carleton.special: Optional arts supplements (visual art ≤20 images, music, theater, dance, film); no creative writing portfolios

swarthmore.platform: Common App, Coalition on Scoir, QuestBridge
swarthmore.prompts: Significant aspects of your identity/background, how your communities shaped you, how you navigate difference; a topic that recently fascinated you and what drives further exploration.
swarthmore.special: Non-U.S.-schooled applicants: Swarthmore Video Response, English proficiency result, or InitialView/Vericant

uc-berkeley.prompts: 4 Personal Insight Questions (350 words each) from 8 prompt options — leadership, creative side, greatest talent/skill, educational opportunity, significant challenge, favorite academic subject, community service, what makes you a strong candidate for UC.
uc-berkeley.special: No ED/EA — UC system has neither. Single RD deadline Nov 30. Recommendations are by admissions invitation only.

uw-seattle.prompts: UW personal statement + additional short-response prompts on academic and personal experiences.
uw-seattle.teacher_recs: Not accepted — UW does not accept letters of recommendation
uw-seattle.special: No ED/EA. Single RD Nov 15 deadline. No letters of recommendation accepted (unusual).

ut-austin.prompts: 1 required essay (topic A: personal experiences), 3-4 short answers on leadership, community, and career goals. Robotics Program applicants add a 500-word robotics essay.
ut-austin.special: Robotics Program requires 500-word robotics essay by Dec 1. Testing is REQUIRED, no superscore.

duke.prompts: Essay 1: Why Duke (250 words). Essay 2: Choose from prompts on personal identity, intellectual curiosity, or community. Optional 3rd essay for QuestBridge or specific majors.
duke.special: Test-optional (not reinstated per CDS C8). Robertson Scholars requires separate application (Nov 15).

texas-am.special: Corps of Cadets separate application; ETAM major placement post-freshman year.

ut-dallas.special: McDermott Scholars requires separate application by Jan 15.
